correctness.rationale: Every word traces a finite connected subtree of the free-group Cayley graph. The tree-covering walk length is exactly twice the edge count minus endpoint distance; varying endpoints according to Green H/R/L/D gives the four formulas. Nested scans retain only logarithmic-size counters; all minima and decisions are in deterministic logspace. value.rationale: The main 2026 paper explicitly asks whether the non-context-free/non-co-context-free D/R/L Green languages can be context-sensitive. Showing they are in deterministic logspace gives a substantially stronger constructive answer for every fixed rank, computes actual minimum lengths as usable invariants, and connects structural Munn-tree geometry to a sharp practical small-space recognition algorithm. The contribution is a synthesis of earlier theorems, not a new free-group normalization theorem.
